examples: Independently constructed cross-domain scenarios. No original reviewer quotations, identities, manuscript measurements or bibliographic details are included.

criteria.title: Internal consistency
criteria.check: Compare numbers, units, labels and conditions across text, tables and captions. Require two comparable passages before suggesting a discrepancy.

example.scenario: A survey summary and its table describe the same group with different counts.
example.question: Could these counts use different inclusion rules?

criteria.suppressWhen: Do not flag differences when populations, units or aggregation differ.

criteria.title: Claims and validation
criteria.check: Ask whether the scope or strength of a claim exceeds the available validation. Distinguish missing evidence from evidence outside the supplied context.

example.scenario: A scheduling method tested on one workload is described as reliable under all operating conditions.
example.question: Would limiting this statement to the tested workload make its support clearer?

criteria.suppressWhen: Do not demand a new experiment when the claim already states the evaluated scope.

criteria.title: Comparison and attribution
criteria.check: Ask whether benefits are compared under the same inputs and evaluation protocol. Separate representation value from predictive improvement and isolate confounding causes.

example.scenario: A forecasting pipeline adds a latent reconstruction but is compared with a direct predictor using a different test split.
example.question: Could a shared test split help separate the benefit of the representation from the evaluation setup?

criteria.suppressWhen: Different goals may justify different methods. Ask about the goal instead of declaring a method unnecessary.

criteria.title: Method choices
criteria.check: Ask why a consequential method, sampling scheme or parameter was chosen and whether the conclusion depends on it.

example.scenario: A document grouping study fixes a sampling budget without connecting it to the measured outcome.
example.question: What evidence would help readers judge whether this sampling budget affects the conclusion?

criteria.suppressWhen: An existing justification or an explicitly limited exploratory design can be sufficient. Do not automatically demand sensitivity experiments.

criteria.title: Flow and repetition
criteria.check: Identify repeated explanations or a missing logical link. Require two passages for a repetition concern.

example.scenario: An algorithm description and a later paragraph repeat the same procedural detail without adding interpretation.
example.question: Could one of these passages point to the other and leave more room for interpreting the result?

criteria.suppressWhen: A concise overview followed by necessary detail is not redundant.

criteria.title: Positioning and support
criteria.check: Ask whether a claim needs support or comparison with related work. Name a paper only when its actual content and bibliographic identity are supplied and verified.

example.scenario: A manuscript states that prior approaches cannot address a task without identifying which approaches or conditions it means.
example.question: Could this claim be tied to specific prior methods and the conditions in which their limitations apply?

criteria.suppressWhen: Never invent references or favour papers because of the author’s editorial role. A bibliography entry alone does not verify what a paper supports.
